title: Two published counts of the turbines, side by side
intro: Switch between the turbine count CNBC says the lawsuit alleges and the count TechCrunch quotes from the Southern Environmental Law Center. The page does not add them, and it does not treat either as the judge’s finding.
note: “27” is what CNBC, on 31 October 2026, says the complaint alleges: turbines installed and operated in Southaven between August and December 2025, without an air permit. “At least 35” is what TechCrunch, the same day, says the Southern Environmental Law Center said, and TechCrunch’s phrase includes other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site, not turbines alone. Judge Debra M. Brown’s order of 30 October does not choose a count and does not find that a permit was missing. The order says the plaintiffs seek a civil penalty of up to $124,426 per day per violation. That number is a request. It is not on this control, because multiplying it by a number of days would invent a total the order does not state. SpaceX did not immediately comment to CNBC.
